decisions.latin: Nonne Deo subjécta erit ánima mea?
decisions.why: *Nonne* asks a question that expects 'yes'; Portuguese does it with a bare *Não …?* (as 13:4 *Não hão de saber todos*), not with *acaso* (the *numquid* row, which expects 'no'). *subjícere → sujeitar* (settled, D43; the row names 61:2 and 61:6). Natural order puts the subject before the predicate; the Latin's order (the soul last) is kept as an option. The colon is the Matins antiphon *Nonne Deo * subjécta erit ánima mea* (Psalmi matutinum, grep): in Portuguese it would split *Não estará a minha alma * sujeita a Deus?*

options.label: Não estará a minha alma sujeita a Deus

forms.nonne: Não estará a minha alma sujeita a Deus

options.label: Não estará sujeita a Deus a minha alma

forms.nonne: Não estará sujeita a Deus a minha alma

options.note: the Latin's order; the colon ends on the soul, as *ánima mea*.

options.label: Porventura a minha alma não estará sujeita a Deus

forms.nonne: Porventura a minha alma não estará sujeita a Deus

options.note: MS1932's build (*Porventura … não há-de estar*); three syllables longer.

decisions.latin: ab ipso enim salutáre meum · quóniam ab ipso patiéntia mea
decisions.why: Both colons are verbless in the Latin (and the Greek, παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ). Portuguese needs a verb; *ab* is 'from', so the verb of coming is what the preposition already says (DRB 'from him is'; MS1932 *dependendo dele*, *dele é que vem*). *dele é* is shorter but is heard as possession ('is his'), which is *Dómini est salus* (3:9), another build. The two verses answer each other (61:2 question, 61:6 command) and keep one verb.

options.label: dele é
options.note: the copula only; heard as belonging.

decisions.latin: Nam et ipse Deus meus, et salutáris meus
decisions.why: The glossary row *étenim / nam et / enim* gives *pois também* (118:24 *Pois também os vossos testemunhos*). Here *et … et* can also be read as 'both … and', and the Greek καὶ γάρ is often just 'for indeed' (DRB drops it: 'For he is my God'). 61:7 says the same line without *et* (*Quia ipse Deus meus*), so the Portuguese keeps the one small difference the Latin has. Risk: *também ele* may be heard as 'he too' (besides another). *Pois ele é tanto o meu Deus como o meu Salvador* (the correlative reading) was weighed and refused: it decides a reading the Latin leaves open and is long.

options.label: Pois ele é
options.note: DRB; the same words as 61:7 after *Porque*; *et* unsaid.

decisions.why: *movéri → ser abalado* (row; 9:27, 29:7 *não serei abalado*). *ámplius* with a negation → *já não* (the *ámplius* row, 38:14 *e já não existirei*); οὐ μὴ … ἐπὶ πλεῖον, DRB 'I shall be moved no more'. *já não* may suggest he was shaken before — that is the Latin's 'no more' too.

options.label: não serei mais abalado
options.note: the same sense, the adverb inside.

decisions.why: *irrúere in* is to rush upon, fall upon (ἐπιτίθεσθε ἐπ᾿, to set upon). *vos lançais sobre* is the plain physical verb, and it is what the Ps 58 draft has for *irruérunt in me* (58:4 *lançaram-se sobre mim os fortes*), so the Latin verb reads the same in both. *Quoúsque → até quando*, as *úsquequo* (row). The plural *vós* is the enemies (rule 3); *vos* here is the reflexive, and 'you all' is named in the next colon, so the address cannot be heard as to God.

decisions.latin: tamquam paríeti inclináto et macériæ depúlsæ
decisions.why: The man attacked is like a wall already leaning and a fence already pushed (φραγμῷ ὠσμένῳ, 'thrust'); the dative says what is done to him. *paries* is the wall of a house → *parede*; *macéria* an enclosure wall (L&S: of a garden, of loose stones), the Greek φραγμός a fence or hedge, DRB 'fence' → *cerca*. *depéllere* is to thrust away or down: *empurrada* keeps the push; *abalado* (MS1932) is taken by *movéri* in 61:3; *derrubada* says it has already fallen, which the Latin does not. Draft 0 had *a um muro empurrado*: checks flagged its final rhyming with 61:3 *abalado* (-ado, no echo in the Latin), so the noun went to *cerca* — the Greek's and DRB's.

options.label: a um muro empurrado
options.note: *muro* for the stone enclosure; rhymes with 61:3 *abalado* at the final.

options.label: a um muro abalado
options.note: MS1932; collides with *movéri → ser abalado* in 61:3.

decisions.why: The row *verúmtamen → todavia* names 61:5–6 and 61:10; three times in the psalm, three times the same word, as Ps 38 did (πλήν each time). The blind reader of Ps 38 heard 'an unclear contrast'; the particle is often asseverative (DRB 'But … But … But').

*cogitáre → pensar em* (working row); with an infinitive, *pensaram em repelir* is natural Portuguese for 'they thought of / had it in mind to'. The Greek ἐβουλεύσαντο is 'took counsel'. The row carries a proposal (from Ps 51) to use *maquinar* where the object is evil; here the object is an act, not a thing plotted, so the row stands. *repéllere* without *a* → *repelir* (settled, D42).

*prétium* is price, worth (τιμή: price, honour). DRB keeps 'my price'; MS1932 interprets *a minha dignidade*; the Hebrew has 'his height'. The Latin word is a price, and the Church's reading of this verse hears in it the price paid for man — so the word stays (rule 2: images and words kept; no explaining). Cost: the ear may find *repelir o meu preço* obscure; the Latin is obscure here too.

options.label: a minha honra
options.note: the other sense of τιμή; *honra* is honor's word (8:6).

decisions.why: The Latin reads *in siti*, 'in thirst' (the Greek text in the parallels has ἐν ψεύδει, 'in falsehood'; the Latin follows a reading with thirst, and the Latin is followed — rule 1). *com sede* is how Portuguese says running while thirsty; MS1932 *corri sedento*.

decisions.latin: ore suo benedicébant, et corde suo maledicébant
decisions.why: *maledícere → amaldiçoar* is settled (D44, from 54:13), and D44 itself names the question this verse raises: whether, where the two stand paired, it must be *maldizer … bendizer*. Here they are paired in one colon, the antithesis is the whole point (mouth / heart, bless / curse), and Latin and Greek both build it on one root (bene- / male-dícere, εὐλογοῦσαν / κατηρῶντο — the Greek does not share the root, the Latin does). *bendiziam … maldiziam* keeps the Latin's echo; *maldizer* is current Portuguese. MS1932 has the same pair. Departure from the row recorded; proposal in the glossary: *maldizer* where *benedícere* stands beside it.

*emigráre* has only one other place, 51:7 (transitive, *te desalojará da tua tenda*, D44), and the row asked 61:7 to decide. Intransitive, it is to move out of one's dwelling (L&S 'to remove, depart from a place'; μεταναστεύσω). The cognate *emigrar* is heard as going abroad (51:7's readers); *mudar-se* is heard as 'change oneself' without a place named; *partir* as dying. *não serei desalojado* keeps 51:7's root and the image of being put out of one's place, and pairs with *já não serei abalado* (61:3), whose Latin is also a steadfast future. Cost: the Latin active becomes a passive, which names an agent the Latin does not (voice is grammar, D2; the enemies of 61:4 are the ones who push).

options.label: não me mudarei
options.note: active, the dwelling image; may be heard as 'I will not change'.

options.label: não emigrarei
options.note: the cognate; heard as going abroad.

options.label: não vacilarei
options.note: MS1932; the sense, not the image.

decisions.why: A vocative. *congregátio → congregação* (the *synagóga* row; D34). *omnis* with a singular is 'the whole'. The *ó* of the vocative row is for colons where the noun could be heard as an object; here *Esperai nele* already has its object, so the bare vocative is clear. The colon is also a versicle said alone (05-01c, Pasc2-3, grep).

options.label: vós todos que constituís o povo

forms.congregatio: vós todos que constituís o povo

decisions.why: *de vanitáte* (ἐκ ματαιότητος) is 'from / by / out of vanity': the means (false weights), the source (they are made of emptiness), or the motive. DRB 'by vanity' keeps the means. *pela vaidade* keeps DRB's openness between means and motive; *por vaidade* would say motive (and conceit); *com o que é vão* says only the means. *vánitas → vaidade* is the working row; readers of four psalms heard conceit first — here the colon's *enganarem* pulls it towards emptiness and deceit. *vani … vanitáte* in the verse echo in *vãos … vaidade*. *ipsi* is *eles*, set first so that the infinitive has its subject.

options.label: com o que é vão
options.note: the row's candidate for emptiness; means only.

decisions.why: D9 deferred; the row proposes *juntos* for persons acting together (33:4 *exaltemos juntos*), *a um só tempo* for one agent or a thing (4:9), and 40:7 had to take *no mesmo sentido*. Here the subject is plural people (*ipsi*, the sons of men) deceiving together — ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, DRB 'together'. So *juntos*, by the row's own proposal. It closes the colon on a paroxytone.

The row *concupíscere → ansiar por* is open and was built on good objects (118:20 the law, 44:12 the King's desire). Here the object is plunder, and the verb is the Decalogue's (*non concupísces*, as the Vulgate of Ex 20:17 is commonly quoted — from memory, unverified), which Portuguese says *cobiçar* (*não cobiçarás*). *ansieis por rapinas* is correct but its subjunctive is rare in the mouth. MS1932 *cobiçar*. Recorded as a local departure; proposal on the row: *cobiçar* where the object is another's goods.
*rapína* (ἅρπαγμα, a thing seized). *rapinas* is the Latin's word and current in *ave de rapina*; *roubos* is plainer but is the acts, not the goods seized. MS1932 *rapinas*.

*afflúere* is to flow towards (ῥέῃ, 'flow'). *afluírem* keeps the flowing image the Latin and the Greek share; *abundarem* (DRB 'abound', MS1932 *se abundardes*) is plainer and loses it. The Latin's order (riches first) becomes a conditional clause in natural order.

decisions.latin: Semel locútus est Deus, duo hæc audívi
decisions.why: The verse turns on 'once … two': *Semel* stands first in the Latin and *Uma vez* first answers *duas coisas*. *Uma vez* at the head can be heard as 'once upon a time'; *Deus falou uma vez* avoids that but loses the chiasm. *eu* is supplied with *ouvi* (D2): bare *estas duas coisas ouvi* after a verse-opening statement can be heard as the *vós* imperative 'hear these two things' (rule 3's homograph, the other way round).

Dative of possession, parallel to *potéstas Dei est*: 'power is God's, and yours, Lord, is mercy'. *e vossa, Senhor, é a misericórdia* keeps the parallel of possession and the turn to address. The verbless *e a vós, Senhor, a misericórdia* is closer to the letter but halts. MS1932 *e tu, Senhor, és misericordioso* changes the noun to an adjective (refused).

decisions.why: *réddere → pagar* (open row: 7:5, 27:4b *pagai-lhes a retribuição*, the vows); *retribuir* is *retribúere*'s. *pagar a cada um* is how Portuguese says rendering to each his due. *tu* is kept as *vós* (the Latin names it).

options.label: dareis
options.note: plain; *dare*'s verb (27:4 *Dai-lhes segundo as suas obras*).

decisions.why: *juxta* (according to) → *conforme* (working row, 118:169), kept apart from *secúndum → segundo* (27:4 *segundo as suas obras*). The Greek is κατά in both; the Latin varies, and Portuguese has a plain pair.

choices.61:2: *enim → pois* (row). *salutáre → salvação* (D6). The colon *Nonne Deo * subjécta erit ánima mea* is a Matins antiphon (grep).
choices.61:3: *salutáris meus* (masculine, of God) → *o meu Salvador* (the *salutáris · salvátor* row: one Greek word, σωτήρ, here and at 61:7). *suscéptor → amparo* (D19; the row names 61:3). 61:3 and 61:7 are one Greek line with two Latin variations (*salutáris / salvátor* merged by the row; *suscéptor / adjútor* kept apart as the glossary keeps them; *non movébor ámplius / non emigrábo* kept apart).
choices.61:4: The whole verse is one question in DO's Latin (the second colon ends with *?*). *interfícitis univérsi vos* → *matais todos vós*: no object supplied, as the Latin; *como a uma parede* then says what is done to the man, the dative's sense. *univérsus → todo* (row).
choices.61:5: *repéllere* (no *a*) → *repelir* (settled, D42). *ore suo … corde suo* → *com a sua boca … com o seu coração* (the article before possessives, rule 5). The Greek has no object 'me' for the verbs, and none is supplied (MS1932 adds *me*).
choices.61:6: *súbditus / subjéctus esse → ser sujeito a* (36:6 *sê sujeito ao Senhor*); the soul addressed is *tu*, as the refrain 41:6 *minha alma* (bare vocative). *patiéntia → paciência* (9:19). The colon echoes 61:2 by design (*estará sujeita / sê sujeita*, *dele vem … dele vem*).
choices.61:8: *está* supplied in the first colon (copula, D2); the Latin's *est* is at the end and stands there. *Deus auxílii mei* is left verbless, an apposition, as the Latin. The verse is a Matins antiphon (*In Deo salutáre meum * et glória mea: et spes mea in Deo est*) and the Alleluia verse of 10-09 (grep). *glória mea* here is of God (the *glória mea* row names 61:8).
choices.61:9: *effúndere → derramar* (settled row names 61:9). *coram → diante de* (50:6, 55:13). *Deus adjútor noster* → *Deus é o nosso auxílio* (copula supplied). *in ætérnum → para sempre* (D23).
choices.61:10: *vani … mendáces* → *vãos são … mentirosos*: the copula supplied once and understood in the second member, as the Latin has none. *in statéris → nas balanças* (ἐν ζυγοῖς), the concrete image. The repeated *os filhos dos homens* is kept (rule 6). The Greek's τοῦ ἀδικῆσαι is not in this Latin, which has *ut decípiant*.
choices.61:11: *Nolíte* ×3 → *Não* ×3: the triple negation is kept; MS1932's calque *Não queirais* is heavier than the prohibition needs. *speráre in → esperar em* (D36). *cor appónere* → *pôr … o coração*, with *nelas* supplied (Portuguese needs where; DRB 'upon them').
choices.61:12: *potéstas → poder* (no row; *virtus* also *poder* — they do not meet in this psalm). *audíre → ouvir*.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (no Diurnal text in the parallels file). Liturgical uses by grep in content/do: Matins antiphons *Nonne Deo * subjécta erit ánima mea* and *In Deo salutáre meum * et glória mea: et spes mea in Deo est*; versicle 61:9a (05-01c, Pasc2-3); Alleluia 61:8 (missa 10-09). Hard readings: 61:5 *prétium meum* (kept as price), *in siti* (Latin against the Greek text's ἐν ψεύδει), 61:10 *de vanitáte in idípsum*, 61:7 *non emigrábo* (the row left it to this psalm). Two local departures from rows, recorded: 61:5 *maldiziam* (D44 *amaldiçoar*), 61:11 *cobiceis* (open row *ansiar por*).

Hard checks pass. First run flagged 61:3 / 61:4 finals rhyming (-ado: abalado / empurrado); 61:4 changed to *a uma cerca empurrada* (decision depulsae). Soft length flags accepted: 61:5a −4 and 61:11a −6 (Portuguese is shorter than the Latin's long verbs; nothing omitted — 61:11 keeps the triple *não*), 61:7b +3 (*não serei desalojado*, the row's verb), 61:8b +3 (the article before possessives and the supplied *o*). No cadence closes on a proparoxytone.
